FSS de banda eliminada a 12 GHz: arreglo periódico de cruces metálicas sobre un sustrato dieléctrico. Excitada por una onda plana con incidencia theta: la incidencia normal simula un cuarto de celda unitaria con condiciones de contorno de simetría, y la incidencia oblicua, una celda unitaria con condiciones de contorno periódicas (de Bloch). Compárese con el 

ejemplo de Tidy3D# %%
import os
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

import gdsfactory as gf
from gdsfactory.technology import LogicalLayer, LayerLevel, LayerStack
import luminescent as lumi
here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))

# simulation folder
path = os.path.join(here, "runs", "FSS")
# lumi.gui()
# raise ValueError(f"Delete {path} to rerun simulation") if os.path.exists(path) else None

# dims [mm]
# length units are arbitrary so long as they're consistent
P = 15  # periodicity
L = 9.4  # length of cross
W = 2.0  # width of cross stub
h_sub = 2.2  # substrate thickness
h_metal = 0.1  # metal thickness

# frequencies [GHz]
# spectrum computed from single FDTD run. more frequencies slightly increases runtime
frequency = 12
bandwidth = 4
nfs = 101
frequencies = np.linspace(frequency - bandwidth / 2, frequency + bandwidth / 2, nfs)

c0 = 300  # speed of light [mm GHz]
wl = c0 / frequency  # wavelength [mm]

# incidence angle [degrees] from z in xz plane. E along y (TE)
theta = 0

def setup(path, frequency, frequencies, P, L, W, h_sub, h_metal, theta):
    # simulation parameters
    dx = .2  # desired resolution near metal
    nres = 6 # not too important for RF problems where dx<<wavelength dominates
    shutoff = 1e-3
    tmax = 1000  # max time [periods]
    PML_decay = 0.0001  # x y z
    courant = 0.9
    subpixel_smoothing = 1
    shot_every = 2.5  # movie [periods]
    views = [lumi.view("Ex",x=0, z=h_metal / 2)]

    # normal incidence: quarter unit cell [0, P/2]² with symmetry walls (E along y: PEC on x, PMC on y)
    # oblique incidence: one full unit cell, periodic in x y. Bloch wavevector sets incidence angle (exact at center frequency)
    sym = theta == 0
    if sym:
        boundaries = ["PEC", "PMC", "PML"]
        k_bloch = None
    else:
        boundaries = ["periodic", "periodic", "PML"]
        k_bloch = lumi.bloch_wavevector(theta, 0, dim=3, f=frequency, c0=c0)

    # margins
    # air gap keeps evanescent resonant field from coupling to PML
    gap = 40.0
    source_offset = 3*wl/nres

    # vertical dims
    z_o1 = h_metal + gap
    z_o2 = -h_sub - gap
    zmin = z_o2
    zmax = z_o1 + source_offset

    # materials
    # refine mesh in substrate and metal: n sets mesh density relative to vacuum
    materials = {**lumi.MATERIALS, "sub": lumi.material(epsilon=2.5,dx=dx), "PEC": lumi.PEC(dx=dx)}
    background = "air"

    # layers
    METAL = 1, 0
    SUB = 2, 0
    layer_stack = LayerStack(
        layers={
            "metal": LayerLevel(
                layer=LogicalLayer(layer=METAL),
                thickness=h_metal,
                zmin=0,
                material="PEC",
                mesh_order=1,
            ),
            "sub": LayerLevel(
                layer=LogicalLayer(layer=SUB),
                thickness=h_sub,
                zmin=-h_sub,
                material="sub",
                mesh_order=2,
            ),
        }
    )

    # make component in gdsfactory. alternatively can import .gds into gdsfactory
    # cross unit cell centered at origin, clipped to quarter cell x, y >= 0 under symmetry
    lo = 0 if sym else -1

    def rect(a, b):
        return [(lo * a, lo * b), (a, lo * b), (a, b), (lo * a, b)]

    c = gf.Component()
    c.add_polygon(rect(W / 2, L / 2), layer=METAL)
    c.add_polygon(rect(L / 2, W / 2), layer=METAL)
    c.add_polygon(rect(P / 2, P / 2), layer=SUB)
    c.plot(return_fig=True).savefig("layout.png")

    bbox = c.bbox_np().tolist()
    bbox[0].append(zmin)
    bbox[1].append(zmax)

    # sources, monitors
    # plane wave on face frame spanning the cell. E along y, H along x
    # wave admittance in air: Hx/Ey = cos(theta) in magnitude (sign fixed automatically)
    frames = [lumi.face("plane_wave", modes=[[{"Ex": 1, "Hy": np.cos(np.deg2rad(theta))}]])]

    # dim: outward normal axis. source injects into cell, monitors record in (-) and out (+) waves
    sources = [
        lumi.source(
            "o1", z_o1 + source_offset, dim=3,
            frame="plane_wave",
            f=frequency,
            bandwidth=max(max(frequencies) - min(frequencies), frequency / 8),
        )
    ]

    monitors = [
        lumi.monitor("o1", z_o1, dim=3, frame="plane_wave"),
        lumi.monitor("o2", z_o2, dim=-3, frame="plane_wave"),
    ]

    # writes .obj mesh files from gdsfactory component
    c.flatten()
    lumi.mesh(path, c, layer_stack, materials, zmin, zmax)

    # writes setup file
    lumi.setup(
        path=path,
        f=frequency,
        fs=frequencies,
        c0=c0,
        materials=materials,
        background=background,
        boundaries=boundaries,
        # k_bloch=k_bloch,
        bbox=bbox,
        #
        frames=frames,
        sources=sources,
        monitors=monitors,
        #
        nres=nres,
        courant=courant,
        PML_decay=PML_decay,
        subpixel_smoothing=subpixel_smoothing,
        # 
        views=views,
        shot_every=shot_every,
        tmax=tmax,
        shutoff=shutoff,
    )


setup(path, frequency, frequencies, P, L, W, h_sub, h_metal, theta)

# %%
lumi.gui()
lumi.solve(path)

import gdsfactory as gf

here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))

w_wg = 0.5
taper_length = 15.0
n_periods = 16
fill_factor = 0.471
fiber_angle = 7.978  # in clad

period = 0.6324
x_offset = -0.815  # fiber shift along x from grating port

h_teeth = .08

        taper_angle=taper_angle,
        wavelength=wavelength,
        fiber_angle=fiber_angle,
        nclad=nclad,
        layer_slab=SLAB,
        cross_section=gf.cross_section.cross_section(width=w_wg, layer=WG),
    )
    wg = c << gf.components.straight(

    )
    wg.connect("o2", gc.ports["o1"])

        component=c,
        layer=BBOX,
        top=margin,
        bottom=margin,
        right=max(0, x_fiber + Dlim / 2 - gc.xmax),
    )
    full_bbox = c.bbox_np().tolist()

    clipper = gf.Component()
    clipper_ref = clipper << gf.components.rectangle(
        size=(full_bbox[1][0] - full_bbox[0][0], full_bbox[1][1]),
        layer=WG,
    )

    half_component = gf.Component()
    clipper_ref.movex(full_bbox[0][0])
    for layer in (WG, SLAB, BBOX):
        clipped = gf.boolean(
            c,
            clipper,
            operation="and",
            layer=layer,
            layer1=layer,
            layer2=WG,
        )
        half_component << clipped
    half_component.add_port("wg", port=wg.ports["o1"])
    half_component.flatten()
    c = half_component
    c.plot(return_fig=True).savefig("layout.png")

    bbox = c.bbox_np().tolist()
    bbox[0][1] = 0
    bbox[0].append(zmin)
    bbox[1].append(zmax)

# sources, monitors
    frames = [
        lumi.plane_frame(
            "wg",
            start=[-w_wg / 2 - margin, -zmargin],
            stop=[0, h_core + zmargin],
            boundaries=[("PML", "PEC"), "PML"],
            wls_mode_solver=[wavelength],
        ),
        lumi.plane_frame(
            "fiber",
            modes=[
                [
                    lumi.gaussian_mode(
                        D_beam,
                        nclad,
                        dx=wavelength / nclad / nres,
                        theta=np.deg2rad(fiber_angle),
                        wl=wavelength,
                        half="y+",
                        Dlim=Dlim,
                    )
                ]
            ],
            start=[-Dlim / 2, 0],
            stop=[Dlim / 2, Dlim / 2],
        ),
    ]

    fiber_origin = [
        gc.ports["o2"].center[0] + x_offset + np.sin(np.deg2rad(fiber_angle)) * fiber_offset,
        0,
        zmax,  # source above fiber monitor, on fiber axis
    ]
    monitor_origin = [  # fiber monitor below source
        gc.ports["o2"].center[0] + x_offset + np.sin(np.deg2rad(fiber_angle)) * zmargin,
        0,
        z_port,
    ]
    fiber_basis = [[1, 0, 0], [0, 1, 0], [0, 0, 1]]
    sources = [
        lumi.source(
            "fiber",
            fiber_origin,
            fiber_basis,
            frame="fiber",
            wl=wavelength,
            bandwidth= wavelength / 8,
        )
    ]
    monitors = [
        lumi.gf_monitor("wg", c, layer_stack, frame="wg"),
        lumi.monitor("fiber", monitor_origin, fiber_basis, frame="fiber"),
    ]

    views = [lumi.view("Ey", y=0, z=h_slab+h_teeth / 2)]
    c.flatten()
    lumi.mesh(path, c, layer_stack, lumi.MATERIALS, zmin, zmax)
    lumi.setup(
        path=path,
        wl=wavelength,
        wls=wavelengths,
        materials=lumi.MATERIALS,

# %%
# best of a 15-simulation Nelder-Mead run over fiber_angle, period, fill_factor, x_offset (commented out below)
fiber_angle, period, fill_factor, x_offset = 8.412, 0.6268, 0.510, -1.081
path = os.path.join(here, "runs", "GC_best")

Reproduce el ejemplo de 

acoplador direccional de Tidy3D. Brazos de silicio (n = 3.48, 0.22 µm de espesor, paredes laterales de 30°) sobre óxido (n = 1.45), con aire encima. El layout proviene del archivo coupler.gds de Tidy3D, dilatado 20 nm por lado. La luz entra por el puerto 1 (abajo a la izquierda). Buscamos la longitud de onda a la que la potencia se divide por igual entre los puertos 3 y 4. Tidy3D reporta 1.53 µm con una transmisión total de 0.990 con un nres=15 equivalente.# %%
import os
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

import gdsfactory as gf
from gdsfactory.technology import LogicalLayer, LayerLevel, LayerStack
import luminescent as lumi
here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))

# Tidy3D's coupler.gds: 0.45 um arms, 0.1 um gap, 4 um coupling length
gds_file = os.path.join(here, "coupler.gds")
dilation = 0.02  # per side, at waveguide bottom
sidewall_angle = 30  # deg from vertical
h_wg = 0.22

# domain, port positions [um]
lx, ly = 17, 7
x_port = 8
y_port = 2
source_offset = 1

# 21 frequencies over 1.4 - 1.7 um
wavelengths = np.sort(1 / np.linspace(1 / 1.7, 1 / 1.4, 21)).tolist()
wavelength = 2 / (1 / 1.4 + 1 / 1.7)

def setup(path,  sidewall_angle=sidewall_angle):
    nres=6
    shutoff = 1e-4
    tmax = 1000  # max time [periods]
    PML_decay = [0.001, 0.01, 0.1]
    shot_every = 10
    boundaries = ["PML", "PML", "PML"]
    zmin, zmax = -1.11, 1.11
    views = [lumi.view("Hz", z=h_wg / 2)]

    background = "air"

    WG = 1, 0
    BOX = 2, 0
    layer_stack = LayerStack(
        layers={
            "core": LayerLevel(
                layer=LogicalLayer(layer=WG),
                thickness=h_wg,
                zmin=0,
                material="Si",
                mesh_order=0,
                sidewall_angle=sidewall_angle,
            ),
            "box": LayerLevel(
                layer=LogicalLayer(layer=BOX),
                thickness=-zmin,
                zmin=zmin,
                material="SiO2",
                mesh_order=1,
            ),
        }
    )

    # import arms, dilate, crop to domain (extended left to fit source)
    gds = gf.import_gds(gds_file)
    dbu = gds.kcl.dbu
    arms = gf.kdb.Region(gds.begin_shapes_rec(gds.kcl.layer(1, 0)))
    arms = arms.sized(round(dilation / dbu))
    xmin = -max(lx / 2, x_port + source_offset)
    window = gf.kdb.Region(gf.kdb.Box(round(xmin / dbu), round(-ly / 2 / dbu), round(lx / 2 / dbu), round(ly / 2 / dbu)))
    c = gf.Component()
    c.add_polygon(arms & window, layer=WG)
    c.add_polygon(window, layer=BOX)

    # o1: input (lower left), o2: upper left, o3: upper right, o4: lower right
    w_wg = 0.45 + 2 * dilation
    for name, x, y, a in [
        ("o1", -x_port, -y_port, 180),
        ("o2", -x_port, y_port, 180),
        ("o3", x_port, y_port, 0),
        ("o4", x_port, -y_port, 0),
    ]:
        c.add_port(name, center=(x, y), width=w_wg, orientation=a, layer=WG)
    c.plot(return_fig=True).savefig("layout.png")

    bbox = c.bbox_np().tolist()
    bbox[0].append(zmin)
    bbox[1].append(zmax)

    frames = [
        lumi.plane_frame(
            "wg",
            start=[-1, -0.5],
            stop=[1, zmax],
            wls_mode_solver=[1.4, wavelength, 1.7],
        )
    ]
    sources = [
        lumi.gf_source(
            "o1", c, layer_stack, source_offset,
            frame="wg",
            wl=wavelength,
            bandwidth=wavelength / 8,
        )
    ]
    monitors = [lumi.gf_monitor(p, c, layer_stack, frame="wg") for p in ["o1", "o2", "o3", "o4"]]

    c.flatten()
    lumi.mesh(path, c, layer_stack, lumi.MATERIALS, zmin, zmax)
    lumi.setup(
        path=path,
        wl=wavelength,
        wls=wavelengths,
        materials=lumi.MATERIALS,
        background=background,
        boundaries=boundaries,
        bbox=bbox,
        frames=frames,
        sources=sources,
        monitors=monitors,
        nres=nres,
        tmax=tmax,
        shutoff=shutoff,
        PML_decay=PML_decay,
        views=views,
        shot_every=shot_every,
    )
    return c

# %%
path = os.path.join(here, "runs", "SOI_coupler")
setup(path)

# %%
lumi.gui()
lumi.solve(path)

# %%
import os
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

import gdsfactory as gf
from gdsfactory.technology import LogicalLayer, LayerLevel, LayerStack
import luminescent as lumi
here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))

# coupler dims
w_wg = 1
gap = 0.25
# length: to be swept 
dx = 15
dy = 5

wavelength = 1.55
bandwidth = 0.1
nwls = 11
wavelengths = np.linspace(wavelength - bandwidth / 2, wavelength + bandwidth / 2, nwls)

def setup(path, wavelength, wavelengths,  length,gap, dx, dy, w_wg):

    nres = 6
    shutoff = 3e-3
    tmax = 1000  # max time [periods]
    PML_decay = [0.001, 0.01, 0.1]
    shot_every = 10

    h_rib = 0.4
    boundaries = ["PML", "PML", "PML"]
    views = [lumi.view("Hz", x=0, z=h_rib / 2)]

    # layer stack dims
    h_slab = 0.2
    margin = 1.5
    source_offset = 2

    sidewall_angle = 15
    zmargin = 1.
    zmin = -h_slab - zmargin
    zmax = h_rib + zmargin

    # anisotropic TFLN: X-cut along y
    ne = 2.14
    no = 2.21
    materials = {
        "LN": lumi.material(epsilon=[[no**2, 0, 0], [0, ne**2, 0], [0, 0, no**2]]),
        "SiO2": lumi.material(1.44),
    }
    background = "SiO2"

    # layers
    WG = 1, 0
    BBOX = 2, 0
    layer_stack = LayerStack(
        layers={
            "rib": LayerLevel(
                layer=LogicalLayer(layer=WG),
                thickness=h_rib,
                zmin=0,
                material="LN",
                mesh_order=0,
                sidewall_angle=sidewall_angle,
            ),
            "slab": LayerLevel(
                layer=LogicalLayer(layer=BBOX),
                thickness=h_slab,
                zmin=-h_slab,
                material="LN",
                mesh_order=1,
            ),
        }
    )

    # make component in gdsfactory. alternatively can import .gds into gdsfactory
    c = gf.Component()

    dut = c << gf.components.coupler(
        gap=gap,
        length=length,
        dx=dx,
        dy=dy,
        cross_section=gf.cross_section.cross_section(width=w_wg),
    )
    s = c << gf.components.straight(length=source_offset, width=w_wg)
    s.connect("o2", dut.ports["o1"])

    c << gf.components.bbox(component=c, layer=BBOX, top=margin, bottom=margin)

    for p in dut.ports:
        c.add_port(p.name, port=p)
    c.flatten()
    c.plot(return_fig=True).savefig("layout.png")

    bbox = c.bbox_np().tolist()
    bbox[0].append(zmin)
    bbox[1].append(zmax)

    lx = w_wg + 2 * margin
    frames = [
        lumi.plane_frame(
            "wg",
            start=[-lx / 2, zmin],

zmin, zmax = -zmargin, h_wg + zmargin

    materials = {
        "Si": lumi.material(n=3.4729, epsilon=8.36218, dispersion=[lumi.lorentzian(3.0, 0, 3.2882)]),
        "SiO2": lumi.material(1.4425),
    }
    WG = 1, 0
    layer_stack = LayerStack(
        layers={
            "core": LayerLevel(

                zmin=0,
                material="Si",
                mesh_order=0,
            ),

    )

    # GDSFactory generic coupler: gap 0.236, length 20, dx 10, dy 4
    dc = gf.components.coupler(gap=0.236, length=20)

    window = gf.kdb.Region(gf.kdb.Box(*(round(v / dbu) for v in (bbox[0][0], bbox[0][1], bbox[1][0], bbox[1][1]))))
    c = gf.Component()
    c.add_polygon(arms & window, layer=WG)

    lumi.mesh(path, c, layer_stack, materials, zmin, zmax)
    lumi.setup(

        wls=wavelengths,
        materials=materials,
        background="SiO2",

        bbox=bbox,
        frames=frames,
        sources=sources,
        monitors=monitors,
        nres=nres,
        tmax=1000,  # periods
        shutoff=1e-4,
        views=[lumi.view("Hz", z=h_wg / 2)],
        shot_every=10,
    )
    return c

@gf.cell
def bend_euler_s45(cross_section="strip"):
    """S-bend from two 45° Euler bends, as in the paper's GDSFactory 7.8 mode_converter"""
    c = gf.Component()
    b = gf.components.bend_euler(angle=45, cross_section=cross_section)
    b1 = c << b
    b2 = c << b
    b2.connect("o1", b1.ports["o2"], mirror=True)
    c.add_port("o1", port=b1.ports["o1"])
    c.add_port("o2", port=b2.ports["o2"])

def setup(path, nres):

    mc = gf.components.mode_converter(gap=0.15, length=20, bend=bend_euler_s45)

def classify(path, frame="mm", wl=1.55):
    """per solved mode: TE fraction (lateral E energy) and lateral parity of the dominant E (+1 even, -1 odd)"""
    out = []
    for i in range(nmodes_mm):
        d = np.load(os.path.join(path, "modes", frame, str(wl), f"{i}.npz"))
        ex, ey = d["Ex"], d["Ey"]
        te = (abs(ex) ** 2).sum() / ((abs(ex) ** 2).sum() + (abs(ey) ** 2).sum())
        a = ex if te > 0.5 else ey
        parity = np.real(np.vdot(a, a[::-1, :])) / np.real(np.vdot(a, a))
        out.append((te, parity))
    return out

    te1 = next(i for i, (te, par) in enumerate(c) if te > 0.5 and par < 0)
    return te0, te1

def resonance(wls_nm, T):
    """lowest-wavelength resonance of normalized T: (λ0, FWHM at half dip depth); deeper dip of a doublet"""
    x = np.arange(wls_nm[0], wls_nm[-1], 0.02)
    y = CubicSpline(wls_nm, T)(x)
    dips = [k for k in range(1, len(y) - 1) if y[k] < y[k - 1] and y[k] <= y[k + 1] and y[k] < 0.5]

    def fwhm(k):
        win = abs(x - x[k]) < 3  # local max within ±3 nm (FSR ≈ 7.5 nm)
        half = (y[win].max() + y[k]) / 2
        l = k
        while y[l] < half:
            l -= 1
        r = k
        while y[r] < half:
            r += 1
        # linear interpolation of the half-level crossings
        xl = x[l] + (half - y[l]) / (y[l + 1] - y[l]) * (x[l + 1] - x[l])
        xr = x[r - 1] + (half - y[r - 1]) / (y[r] - y[r - 1]) * (x[r] - x[r - 1])
        return xr - xl

    pair = [d for d in dips if x[d] - x[dips[0]] < 2]  # doublet halves lie within 2 nm
    k = min(pair, key=lambda d: y[d])
    return x[k], fwhm(k)

Dibuje el dispositivo como un componente de gdsfactory (o importe un .gds) con puertos, junto con un LayerStack que asigne espesor y material a cada capa.

Defina materials, frames, sources y monitors.

lumi.mesh(path, c, layer_stack, materials, zmin, zmax) escribe mallas 3D en la carpeta de simulación path.

lumi.setup(path, ...) escribe el problema de simulación y resuelve los modos de los puertos.

lumi.solve(path) ejecuta el FDTD. Se ejecuta en el servidor Colab de Lumi.

lumi.movie(path) muestra la película del campo; sol = lumi.load(path) carga los resultados.

Las unidades de longitud son arbitrarias, pero deben ser coherentes: p. ej., um para fotónica, mm para RF.

Fotónica: wl (central) y wls (longitudes de onda de los resultados) en unidades de longitud.

RF: f y fs con c0, la velocidad de la luz en sus unidades, p. ej., c0=300 para mm y GHz.

Los resultados son arrays sobre wls o fs, en el orden indicado.

Los tiempos (tmax, shot_every, t0) se expresan en periodos de la frecuencia central.

Una sola ejecución calcula todo el espectro; añadir más longitudes de onda apenas aumenta el tiempo de ejecución.

nres: puntos de malla por longitud de onda en el material. 6 es un buen punto de partida para fotónica. La convergencia suele ser <1% a partir de nres=8.

¡Mantenga nres bajo! Gracias a los tensores de suavizado subpíxel, Lumi puede lograr una precisión comparable con un nres menor. El tiempo de ejecución escala como O(N^4) y el tamaño del dominio como O(N^3). Un nres alto es inútil y superará el límite de celdas del nivel gratuito. Nivel gratuito: nres ≤ 8.

La malla se adapta al n de cada material; subpixel_smoothing promedia las fronteras entre materiales: 1 anisótropo (preciso), 0 promedio volumétrico escalar (estable), y valores intermedios una mezcla; las fronteras PEC usan ponderación conforme de aristas (Yu–Mittra).

Compruebe la convergencia aumentando nres hasta que los resultados dejen de cambiar.

Use la simetría para reducir el dominio a la mitad: frontera PMC o PEC en un lado, p. ej., ("PMC", "PML").

Las estructuras cortadas en el borde de bbox continúan sin cambios más allá de él; p. ej., una guía de onda que termina en el borde penetra en la PML como una guía de onda infinita. Los puertos pueden situarse en el borde.

lumi.material(n) o lumi.material(epsilon=...): permitividad relativa, escalar o tensor 3x3 para materiales anisótropos.

También mu, sigma (unidades relativas: multiplique S/m por 377 * (characteristic wavelength in m)), chi2, chi3, dispersion: lista de términos lumi.lorentzian, lumi.drude o lumi.gain (convención de Meep).

n también fija la densidad de malla relativa al vacío; por defecto sqrt(epsilon * mu). Auméntelo, o fije dx (espaciado máximo de malla en unidades geométricas), para refinar la malla en un material, p. ej., metales delgados. dx solo refina, nunca hace la malla más gruesa.

lumi.PEC(n): conductor perfecto para metales.

lumi.placeholder_material(n): se malla pero no tiene propiedades físicas, p. ej., regiones de diseño.

lumi.MATERIALS: biblioteca, p. ej., MATERIALS["Si"] (n constante) o MATERIALS["Si_dispersive"], "SiO2_Malitson", "Au_Rakic" (ajustes dispersivos, requieren length_unit en setup, p. ej., 1e-6 para µm).

materials es un diccionario de nombre a material; las capas de LayerStack y background hacen referencia a estos nombres.

Marco de coordenadas con regiones o puntos de muestreo, reutilizable por cualquier número de fuentes y monitores en distintas posiciones mediante frame="name". Pase todos los marcos a setup(frames=...).

Coordenadas locales: origen en el origin de la fuente o del monitor, ejes según su base. mirror="x" (o "y") refleja respecto a x=0 (o y=0) local, p. ej., para un puerto en el lado opuesto de un dispositivo simétrico.

Tipos y resultados:

plane_frame: sección transversal del puerto con modos resueltos. Resultados modal, flux, power. Las fuentes necesitan uno.

points_frame: campos en puntos, o integrales sensor="voltage" / "current" para RF.

box_frame: campos en un volumen muestreado.

cage_frame: superficie de caja cerrada. Flujo por cara, potencia, campo lejano.

spherical_frame: esfera de radio r. Flujo, potencia, campo lejano si está cerrada.

Por defecto, los resultados están en el dominio de la frecuencia en wls o fs; time_domain=True registra en su lugar señales temporales.

Los nombres de fuentes y monitores coinciden con los nombres de puertos de gdsfactory, p. ej. "o1". gf_source y gf_monitor los colocan en los puertos.

Constructores generales source monitor

Filas de la base del puerto: x local, y local, normal hacia afuera. Las fuentes inyectan de forma bidireccional.

Resultados de los monitores: sol["monitors"][name]["modal"][mode number]["+" or "-"], donde "+" es saliente (a lo largo de la normal) y "-" entrante.

Los S-parameters son cocientes de amplitudes modales, p. ej.S21 = sol["monitors"]["o2"]["modal"][0]["+"] / sol["monitors"]["o1"]["modal"][0]["-"]
S11 = sol["monitors"]["o1"]["modal"][0]["+"] / sol["monitors"]["o1"]["modal"][0]["-"]

Los objetivos de diseño inverso usan "port@mode±", p. ej. lumi.target("o1@0-", "o2@0+", 1).

import os
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

import gdsfactory as gf
from gdsfactory.technology import LogicalLayer, LayerLevel, LayerStack
import luminescent as lumi
here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))

# simulation folder
root = os.path.join(here, "runs")

# dims [um]
# length units are arbitrary so long as they're consistent
P = 0.7  # periodicity, subwavelength in substrate (P < wavelength / n_sub) so no diffraction
h = 1.0  # pillar height
radii = np.linspace(0.08, 0.3, 4)  # pillar radii to sweep

# wavelengths [um]
# spectrum computed from single FDTD run. more wavelengths slightly increases runtime
wavelength = 1.55
bandwidth = 0.1
nwls = 11
wavelengths = np.linspace(wavelength - bandwidth / 2, wavelength + bandwidth / 2, nwls)

# quarter circle polygon
def quarter_circle(r, n=32):
    t = np.linspace(0, np.pi / 2, n)
    return [(0, 0)] + list(zip(r * np.cos(t), r * np.sin(t)))

def setup(path, wavelength, wavelengths, P, h, r, plot=False):
    # simulation parameters
    nres = 6
    shutoff = 3e-3
    tmax = 1000  # max time [periods]
    PML_decay = 0.001
    subpixel_smoothing = 1
    courant=.7
    shot_every = 10  # movie [periods]
    views = [lumi.view("Ex", y=0, z=h / 2)]

    # simulate 1/4 unit cell. x- y- are symmetry planes, x+ y+ are periodic cell edges (also symmetry planes)
    # Ex polarized normal incidence: PEC on x walls, PMC on y walls
    boundaries = ["PEC", "PMC", "PML"]

    # margins
    # gap keeps evanescent near field away from monitors
    gap = 1.0
    source_offset = 0.5

    # vertical dims. illuminated from substrate side, transmits into air
    z_o1 = -gap
    z_o2 = h + gap
    zmin = z_o1 - source_offset
    zmax = z_o2

    # materials
    background = "air"
    materials = lumi.MATERIALS
    dx=.02
    materials["Si"]['dx']=dx

    # layers
    PILLAR = 1, 0
    SUB = 2, 0
    layer_stack = LayerStack(
        layers={
            "pillar": LayerLevel(
                layer=LogicalLayer(layer=PILLAR),
                thickness=h,
                zmin=0,
                material="Si",
                mesh_order=1,
            ),
            "sub": LayerLevel(
                layer=LogicalLayer(layer=SUB),
                thickness=-zmin,
                zmin=zmin,
                material="SiO2",
                mesh_order=2,
            ),
        }
    )

    # make component in gdsfactory
    # 1/4 of pillar unit cell
    c = gf.Component()
    c.add_polygon(quarter_circle(r), layer=PILLAR)
    c.add_polygon([(0, 0), (0, P / 2), (P / 2, P / 2), (P / 2, 0)], layer=SUB)
    if plot:
        c.plot(return_fig=True).savefig("layout.png")

    bbox = c.bbox_np().tolist()
    bbox[0].append(zmin)
    bbox[1].append(zmax)

    # sources, monitors
    # normally incident plane wave over 1/4 cell: Ex, Hy uniform. Hy = n Ex in medium of index n
    nx = ny = round(P / 2 / dx)
    a = np.ones((nx, ny))
    frames = [
        lumi.plane_frame(
            "sub_wave",
            start=[0, 0],
            stop=[P / 2, P / 2],
            boundaries=["PEC", "PMC"],
            modes=[[{"Ex": a, "Hy": materials["SiO2"]["n"] * a}]],
        ),
        lumi.plane_frame(
            "air_wave",
            start=[0, 0],
            stop=[P / 2, P / 2],
            boundaries=["PEC", "PMC"],
            modes=[[{"Ex": a, "Hy": a}]],
        ),
    ]

    # basis rows: local x, local y, outward normal
    basis_top = [[1, 0, 0], [0, 1, 0], [0, 0, 1]]
    basis_bottom = [[-1, 0, 0], [0, 1, 0], [0, 0, -1]]

    sources = [
        lumi.source(
            "o1", [0, 0, z_o1 - source_offset], basis_bottom,
            frame="sub_wave",
            mirror="x",
            wl=wavelength,
            bandwidth=max(max(wavelengths) - min(wavelengths), wavelength / 8),
        )
    ]

    monitors = [
        lumi.monitor("o1", [0, 0, z_o1], basis_bottom, frame="sub_wave", mirror="x"),
        lumi.monitor("o2", [0, 0, z_o2], basis_top, frame="air_wave"),
    ]

    # writes .obj mesh files from gdsfactory component
    c.flatten()
    lumi.mesh(path, c, layer_stack, materials, zmin, zmax)

    # writes setup file
    lumi.setup(
        path=path,
        wl=wavelength,
        wls=wavelengths,
        materials=materials,
        background=background,
        boundaries=boundaries,
        bbox=bbox,
        #
        frames=frames,
        sources=sources,
        monitors=monitors,
        #
        nres=nres,
        PML_decay=PML_decay,
        subpixel_smoothing=subpixel_smoothing,
        courant=courant,
        #
        views=views,
        shot_every=shot_every,
        tmax=tmax,
        shutoff=shutoff,
    )

paths = [os.path.join(root, f"r{r:.3f}") for r in radii]
for i, (path, r) in enumerate(zip(paths, radii)):
    setup(path, wavelength, wavelengths, P, h, r, plot=i == len(radii) - 1)

# %%
for path in paths:
    lumi.solve(path)

# %%
# S21 at center wavelength for each radius
mid = nwls // 2
S21 = []
for path in paths:
    sol = lumi.load(path)
    o1 = sol["monitors"]["o1"]
    o2 = sol["monitors"]["o2"]
    # + denotes outgoing mode (wrt port monitor outward normal), - incoming
    S21.append((o2["modal"][0]["+"] / o1["modal"][0]["-"])[mid])
S21 = np.array(S21)

# transmission relative to smallest pillar, oriented so larger pillars mean more phase delay
t = S21 / S21[0]
if np.unwrap(np.angle(t))[-1] < 0:
    t = np.conj(t)
delay = np.unwrap(np.angle(t))
print(f"phase coverage: {delay.max() - delay.min():.2f} rad ({(delay.max() - delay.min()) / (2 * np.pi):.2f} x 2pi)")

# %%
D = 20  # lens diameter [um]
f = 20  # focal length [um]

# library transmission normalized to max amplitude
lib = t * np.abs(S21) / np.abs(S21).max()

PILLAR = 1, 0
lens = gf.Component()
xs = np.arange(-D / 2, D / 2 + P / 2, P)
for x in xs:
    for y in xs:
        rho = np.hypot(x, y)
        if rho > D / 2:
            continue
        # center delayed most: edge rays travel farther to focus
        target = np.exp(-1j * 2 * np.pi / wavelength * (np.hypot(rho, f) - f))
        r = radii[np.argmin(np.abs(lib - target))]
        tt = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, 64, endpoint=False)
        lens.add_polygon(list(zip(x + r * np.cos(tt), y + r * np.sin(tt))), layer=PILLAR)

lens.plot(return_fig=True).savefig("lens.png")
lens.write_gds(os.path.join(root, "metalens.gds"))

i = np.searchsorted(t, t0)
y[:i] = 0

import subprocess

# harmonic inversion of the ringdown (needs harminv: sudo apt install harminv)
# time is in periods of `wavelength`, so frequency f = wavelength / λ

dt = t[1] - t[0]
out = subprocess.run(["harminv", "-t", str(dt), f"{fmin}-{fmax}"],
                     input="\n".join(map(str, y[i:])), capture_output=True, text=True).stdout

# columns: frequency, decay constant, Q, |amplitude|, phase, error
for line in out.splitlines()[1:]:

    if fmin <= f <= fmax:
        print(f"{1000 * wavelength / f:.2f}nm   Q = {Q:.0f}   |amp| = {amp:.2g}   error = {err:.1e}")

Filtro de rechazo de banda con stub de cuarto de onda en microtira de RF con muesca nominal a 5GHz# %%
import os
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

import gdsfactory as gf
from gdsfactory.technology import LogicalLayer, LayerLevel, LayerStack
import luminescent as lumi
here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))

# simulation folder
path = os.path.join(here, "runs", "stub_filter")

# dims [mm]
# length units are arbitrary so long as they're consistent
w_line = 1.52  # strip width
h_metal = 0.035  # metal thickness
h_sub = 0.8  # substrate thickness
v_rel = 87.5 / 139  # relative signal speed, from microstrip calculator

# frequencies [GHz]
# spectrum computed from single FDTD run. more frequencies slightly increases runtime
frequency = 5
bandwidth = 4
nfs = bandwidth * 25+1
frequencies = np.linspace(frequency - bandwidth / 2, frequency + bandwidth / 2, nfs)

c0 = 300  # speed of light [mm GHz]

# quarter-wave stub at center frequency
l_stub = c0 / frequency * v_rel / 4
l_feed = l_stub

def setup(path, frequency, frequencies, w_line, h_metal, h_sub, l_stub, l_feed):
    # simulation parameters
    nres = 16
    dx = h_sub / 6  # desired resolution in metal
    shutoff = 1e-2
    tmax = 1000  # max time [periods]
    PML_decay = [0.001,.1,.1]
    courant = 0.9
    shot_every =.5 # movie [periods]

    # margins
    zmargin =margin = 5 * h_sub
    source_offset = 5 * h_sub

    # ground plane as PEC boundary on z-
    boundaries = ["PML", "PML", ("PEC", "PML")]

    # vertical dims
    zmin = -h_sub
    zmax = h_metal + zmargin

    views = [
        lumi.view("Ez", x=-source_offset, y=0, z=-h_sub / 2),
        lumi.view("Hz", z=h_metal / 2),
    ]

    # materials
    # refine mesh in metal: n sets mesh density relative to vacuum
    n = (c0 / frequency / nres) / dx
    materials = {**lumi.MATERIALS, "PEC": lumi.PEC(n)}
    background = "air"

    # layers
    TRACE = 1, 0
    SUB = 10, 0
    layer_stack = LayerStack(
        layers={
            "trace": LayerLevel(
                layer=LogicalLayer(layer=TRACE),
                thickness=h_metal,
                zmin=0,
                material="PEC",
                mesh_order=10,
            ),
            "sub": LayerLevel(
                layer=LogicalLayer(layer=SUB),
                thickness=h_sub,
                zmin=-h_sub,
                material="FR4",
                mesh_order=30,
            ),
        }
    )

    # make component in gdsfactory. alternatively can import .gds into gdsfactory
    c = gf.Component()
    feed = c << lumi.straight(length=l_feed, width=w_line, layer=TRACE)
    stub = c << lumi.straight(length=l_stub, width=w_line, layer=TRACE)
    stub.rotate(90)
    stub.movex(l_feed / 2)
    stub.movey(-w_line / 2)
    s = c << lumi.straight(length=source_offset, width=w_line, layer=TRACE)
    s.connect("o2", feed.ports["o1"])

    c << gf.components.bbox(component=c, layer=SUB, top=margin, bottom=margin)

    c.add_port("o1", port=feed.ports["o1"])
    c.add_port("o2", port=feed.ports["o2"])
    c.plot(return_fig=True).savefig("layout.png")

    bbox = c.bbox_np().tolist()
    bbox[0].append(zmin)
    bbox[1].append(zmax)

    # sources, monitors
    # quasi-TEM microstrip mode: ground plane (y-) and strip ("trace" layer) as metal
    w_port = w_line + 2 * margin
    frames = [
        lumi.plane_frame(
            "line_mode",
            start=[-w_port / 2, zmin],  # local xy basis, local y=0 at global zmin of port layer
            stop=[w_port / 2, h_metal + margin],
            metallic_boundaries=["y-", "trace"],
            nmodes=1,
            modes="auto",
            fs_mode_solver=[frequency],
        ),
    ]

    sources = [
        lumi.gf_source(
            "o1", c, layer_stack, source_offset,
            frame="line_mode",
            f=frequency,
            bandwidth=max(max(frequencies) - min(frequencies), frequency / 8),
        )
    ]

    monitors = [
        lumi.gf_monitor("o1", c, layer_stack, frame="line_mode"),
        lumi.gf_monitor("o2", c, layer_stack, frame="line_mode"),
    ]

    # writes .obj mesh files from gdsfactory component
    c.flatten()
    lumi.mesh(path, c, layer_stack, materials, zmin, zmax)

    # writes setup file
    lumi.setup(
        path=path,
        f=frequency,
        fs=frequencies,
        c0=c0,
        materials=materials,
        background=background,
        boundaries=boundaries,
        bbox=bbox,
        #
        frames=frames,
        sources=sources,
        monitors=monitors,
        #
        nres=nres,
        courant=courant,
        PML_decay=PML_decay,
        #
        views=views,
        shot_every=shot_every,
        tmax=tmax,
        shutoff=shutoff,
        device="gpu",
    )

setup(path, frequency, frequencies, w_line, h_metal, h_sub, l_stub, l_feed)

# %%
lumi.gui()
lumi.solve(path)
